title: AGENTS.md
text: dg_list_datasets(q = NULL, n = 1000, schema_only = FALSE) -> tibble columns title, id, description, slug, n_resources, formats, has_table, has_schema. q server-side full-text search; n = Inf fetches whole catalog; schema_only = TRUE keeps datasets declaring schema. dg_pull_dataset(id, remove_na = FALSE) -> named list tibbles (first parseable resource; ZIP yields one element per file). Every table gets trailing .id column. dg_refetch(id, remove_na = FALSE) -> single tibble re-fetched composed id. dg_schema(id) -> tibble (name, title, description, type, example) table’s documented columns, schema_title/schema_name attributes; NULL + message resource declares schema; errors resource found. Input composed table id. get_summary(x, name = NULL) -> one-row metrics tibble: dataset, size_kb, n_vars, n_numeric, n_non_numeric, n_rows, prop_missing. summarise_datasets(datasets = NULL, n = 100) -> metrics many tables. Accepts named list tibbles, nested list (ZIP), dg_list_datasets() tibble, character vector ids, NULL (first n catalog). dg_download_many(ids, remove_na = FALSE) -> list(datasets, metrics). Note: format_tibble() exported (used internally tests).

title: AGENTS.md
text: Composed table id. parsed table’s address <dataset_id>::<resource_id> (single file) <dataset_id>::<resource_id>::<file> (file inside ZIP). dataset_id 24-hex ObjectId, resource_id UUID, <file> base name; :: never appears fields. Built platform’s identifiers, stable re-fetchable, unlike human-readable titles. Stored trailing .id column dg_pull_dataset(); dg_refetch() dg_schema() consume . Injected parsing low-level readers stay untouched. Format handling — two lists, deliberately different. - catalog_formats() = c("csv", "csv.gz", "xls", "xlsx", "parquet") — official tabular formats data.gouv.fr indexes. discovery catalog (dg_list_datasets()) restricted every listed dataset principle openable table. - supported_formats() = c("zip", "csv", "csv.gz", "xls", "xlsx", "parquet",   "tsv", "txt", "json") — everything direct pull can parse. JSON/TSV/TXT intentionally catalog (guaranteed tabular) remain parseable addressed directly. Schema resolution. data.gouv attaches schema pointer (resource$schema = {name, url, version}). dg_schema() resolves pointer — url directly, name via resolve_schema_url() schema.data.gouv.fr — Table Schema document returns fields. Real per-column descriptions live , main API (coverage surveyed: ~36.9% datasets tabular, ~5.1% carry schema pointer, ~4.5% ). Schemas inconsistent: omit per-field title description; field_attr() coerces absent/empty values NA (jsonlite turns empty description=NULL {}, .e. zero-length list, NULL — handle ). Metrics .id column. get_summary()/summarise_datasets() exclude .id metadata column n_vars/n_numeric/n_non_numeric/ prop_missing — address, data variable.

title: Design proposal — discovery-first refresh
text: tibble returned dg_pull_dataset() gains trailing id column holding composed ID. Injected dg_pull_dataset() read_resource()/format_tibble(), low-level parsers stay untouched. Non-ZIP: one element, table gets dataset$id::resource$id. ZIP: one element per file, gets dataset$id::resource$id::<file>. Tradeoff flag: id column inflate n_vars skew prop_missing get_summary(). Mitigation: get_summary()/summarise_datasets() recognize metadata column (reserved name id) exclude n_vars, n_numeric, n_non_numeric, prop_missing.

title: Design proposal — discovery-first refresh
text: Re-fetch exact table addressed composed ID return one tibble (ID addresses single table, multi-file list). Steps: 1. Split id :: → dataset_id (+ optional resource_id + file). 2. fetch_dataset(dataset_id). 3. Locate resource resource_id; error absent. 4. Read ; file segment present, unpack ZIP parse file (needs new read_one_zip_file(zip, file) helper); otherwise read_resource(resource). 5. format_tibble(..., remove_na) return single tibble. Validation: reject malformed IDs (wrong segment count / non-hex dataset id) clear message.

title: Design proposal — discovery-first refresh
text: dg_list_datasets() currently keeps title/id/description/slug discards resources, students can’t tell whether hit holds real table. Fix: keep resources metadata derive compact availability summary. New columns returned tibble: n_resources — number resources (integer; 0 none). formats — comma-joined, de-duplicated, uppercase formats dataset’s resources, e.g. "CSV, ZIP", "—" none. (Reuse supported_formats().) has_table — logical: TRUE resource directly parseable (non-ZIP supported format). ZIP maybe, shown formats set has_table. Adding makes dg_list_datasets(q = "vélo", n = 20) immediately answer “can actually open?” spending download. Note: fetch_datasets_page currently requests format = c("csv","xlsx","tsv","txt") — search already biased tabular formats, resource-level formats still worth surfacing.

what: Main API vs tabular API: division of labour
title: Design proposal — discovery-first refresh
text: Answering “main API even useful tabular API also serves data?”: yes — main API backbone; tabular API variable-metadata supplement. substitutes. Implications package: dg_list_datasets(q) remains irreplaceable: tabular API keyword search, discovery metadata (dataset interest?) comes main API. educational core rests main API. pull path (read_resource) keeps downloading raw files . preserves full format/coverage (xlsx, json, zip; resources tabular service hasn’t indexed), tabular API guarantee. tabular API’s unique value variable metadata pull time, main API lacks. Use supplement : resource served tabular service, /profile/ (optionally /swagger/) gives column names/types/formats + row count user commits full download. 404s, fall back gracefully (column profile). Keying lines ID design: tabular API addressed resource$id (UUID), profile carries dataset_id, composed table ID maps straight onto <dataset_id>::<resource_id>(::<file>) address.

what: New phase: variable/profile pull (via tabular API)
title: Design proposal — discovery-first refresh
text: dg_schema(id) — best-effort column profile single table address. Input: composed table ID (format dg_refetch), raw resource UUID. Implementation: hit https://tabular-api.data.gouv.fr/api/resources/{rid}/profile/ (using resource UUID extracted ID), map columns_fields tibble column, type, format, score, plus total_lines, encoding, separator. Returns NULL (message) resource served tabular API (404), errors malformed ID.

title: Design proposal — discovery-first refresh
text: Baseline (implemented): ID column + dg_refetch() + wrapper_datasets() -> dg_download_many() rename + metrics exclusion + tests. Search surfacing (implemented): dg_list_datasets() availability columns + tests. Preview loop (implemented): summarise_datasets() accepts list-datasets tibble + tests. Column profile (implemented): dg_schema(id) via tabular API /profile/, 404 fallback + tests. (Optional) convenience tweaks.

title: Finding, judging and re-fetching French open data with datagouv
text: datagouv small R client public API data.gouv.fr, French government’s open data platform. written specific user mind: student data scientist wants find dataset matches interests, judge whether usable analysis, download , later re-fetch exact table reproducible way. four steps may sound trivial, platform makes harder : Finding. Enumerating “” published datasets means paging tens thousands records. catalog search server-side matches titles descriptions, free-form often uninformative. Judging. tabular API provides human-readable variable descriptions. actual descriptions live separate schema documents schema.data.gouv.fr; data.gouv.fr attaches pointer (name / url) resource. Without resolving pointer, tell whether column really means assume. Downloading. Datasets come many formats (CSV, Excel, ZIP, Parquet, JSON…), declared format always accurate, “dataset” may contain several files. Re-fetching. Catalog titles even ordering change time, script reaches dataset “title” fragile. want address always resolves table. datagouv addresses four. functions organised around workflow: approach mirrors several US cities propose (e.g. nycOpenData New York), tailored data.gouv.fr API.

title: Finding, judging and re-fetching French open data with datagouv
text: dg_pull_dataset() downloads first parseable tabular resource dataset returns named list tibbles: things know pulling: Supported formats csv, csv.gz, xls, xlsx, parquet, tsv, txt json. ZIP resource unpacked every contained file one formats parsed — one element returned list per file. delimiter CSV/TXT resources auto-detected (comma, semicolon, tab, pipe, …), standard European-style files (semicolon / decimal-comma) handled without configuration. Declared formats always accurate, candidate may fail parse (e.g. json resource actually serves API metadata document). dg_pull_dataset() skips non-parseable resources falls back next tabular one instead erroring. Every returned table carries trailing .id column — stable, unique address.
code: tables <- dg_pull_dataset("6397c0ff56d3963118a18345") names(tables) head(tables[[1]])

title: Finding, judging and re-fetching French open data with datagouv
text: get_summary() computes metrics single table: reported columns dataset (label), size_kb (-memory weight), n_vars, n_numeric, n_non_numeric, n_rows prop_missing (proportion missing values). .id column added dg_pull_dataset() excluded metrics — address, data variable. summarise_datasets() applies get_summary() collection tables. flexible input, accepting: named list tibbles (element single table), named list lists, returned dg_pull_dataset() / dg_download_many() (ZIP may contribute several tables), tibble dg_list_datasets() (dataset downloaded summarised), character vector identifiers (exact titles), NULL download summarise first n datasets catalog. dg_download_many() bundles two common operations: download several datasets return raw tibbles metrics.
code: get_summary(iris, name = "iris") # A tibble: 1 × 7   dataset size_kb n_vars n_numeric n_non_numeric n_rows prop_missing   <chr>     <dbl>  <int>     <int>         <int>  <int>        <dbl> 1 iris       7.09      5         4             1    150            0 # In-memory tables — no network needed summarise_datasets(datasets = list(iris = iris, mtcars = mtcars)) # A tibble: 2 × 7   dataset size_kb n_vars n_numeric n_non_numeric n_rows prop_missing * <chr>     <dbl>  <int>     <int>         <int>  <int>        <dbl> 1 iris       7.09      5         4             1    150            0 2 mtcars     7.04     11        11             0     32            0 out <- dg_download_many(c("6397c0ff56d3963118a18345")) out$metrics head(out$datasets[[1]])

title: Finding, judging and re-fetching French open data with datagouv
text: Putting together, typical session : table id key reproducibility: save , dg_refetch(tbl_id) give table , matter public catalog changes meantime.
code: # 1. Find a documented dataset on a topic of interest. hits <- dg_list_datasets(q = "recharge électrique", schema_only = TRUE, n = 5) hits[, c("title", "has_table")]  # 2. Pull the first one and confirm its columns are documented. tables <- dg_pull_dataset(hits$id[[1]]) tbl_id <- tables[[1]]$.id[1] dg_schema(tbl_id)  # 3. Look at the table and store its stable id for later. head(tables[[1]])  # 4. Re-fetch the exact same table in a later session. again <- dg_refetch(tbl_id)

title: List datasets available on data.gouv.fr — dg_list_datasets
text: Fetching every dataset platform means paging tens thousands records hundreds HTTP requests slow fragile, default deliberately bounded. Set n = Inf return titles regardless count.

title: datagouv 0.0.0.9000
text: Initial development version. dg_list_datasets() lists datasets available data.gouv.fr returns tibble title, id, description slug. format_tibble() converts data frame tibble can drop rows containing missing values. get_summary() computes key metrics (weight, number variables, number rows, missing-value proportion) dataset. summarise_datasets() computes summary metrics collection datasets, disambiguating duplicate titles output appending dataset’s id. dg_pull_dataset() downloads dataset stable, unique id (, fallback, exact title) parses . read_resource() auto-detects delimiter CSV/TXT resources (comma, semicolon, tab, pipe, …) dispatches matching readr reader (read_csv(), read_csv2() European files, read_tsv(), read_delim()), adds support JSON resources (array newline-delimited) via jsonlite. wrapper_datasets() downloads several datasets id returns raw tables summary metrics. dg_download_many() replaces wrapper_datasets() (renamed); wrapper_datasets() longer available. dg_pull_dataset() now tags every returned table stable, unique id column form <dataset>::<resource> (<dataset>::<resource>::<file> file inside ZIP), built platform’s identifiers. dg_refetch() re-fetches single table composed id, reproducibly returning table across calls. dg_list_datasets() now also reports n_resources (file count), formats (distinct file formats) has_table (whether resource can parsed table) dataset. summarise_datasets() accepts tibble returned dg_list_datasets() (identified id column) summarises matching datasets. dg_schema() returns documented column metadata (name, title, description, type, example) declared dataset’s data schema schema.data.gouv.fr, resolved resource’s schema pointer, NULL (message) resource carries schema. dg_list_datasets() now reports has_schema (whether least one resource carries pointer declared data schema) gains schema_only argument keep schema-documented datasets. discovery catalog (dg_list_datasets()) now restricted data.gouv’s official tabular formats (csv, csv.gz, xls, xlsx, parquet) every listed dataset principle openable table. supported_formats() now also parses xls (legacy Excel) parquet resources; nanoparquet new hard dependency. get_summary() summarise_datasets() exclude .id column variable missing-value metrics. dg_pull_dataset() now skips dataset resource whose declared format actually parsed table (e.g. json resource serving API metadata document) falls back next tabular resource, instead erroring first candidate. read_json_file() now reports clear, actionable error top-level JSON object tabular data (e.g. API metadata document variable-length fields) rather cryptic tibble-size error.
